text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment too short, no MDE/power, customer-level randomization","detail":"The test runs for only 1 week, below the 14-day minimum, and states no MDE or power calculation. Storm events are sporadic, so a 1-week window may include few or no storms. Randomizing by customer can also leak between arms, since customers share couriers, routes, and capacity during the same storm.","evidence_quote":"A/B test randomized by customer. Run for 1 week. Compare on-time rate between arms.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Run at least 14 days (long enough to capture sufficient storm events). Define the MDE and power. Randomize at a unit that avoids interference, such as zone or delivery station, ideally with a storm-trigger-conditioned analysis."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing customer experience guardrails for promise window changes","detail":"Widening promise windows changes customer-facing delivery promises, but the only guardrail is Cost Per Delivery. Metrics that would show customer harm from longer promises, such as conversion/order cancellation rate or customer satisfaction/contact rate, are absent. The cost guardrail also has no numeric threshold.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: must not increase.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as checkout conversion, order cancellation rate, and customer contact rate or CSAT. Give each a numeric tolerance threshold, including for Cost Per Delivery."},{"type":"PRIOR_ART","title":"Prior experiment EXP-014 referenced without learnings","detail":"The proposal cites EXP-014 as a predecessor but does not state its outcome or what was learned. It also does not explain why a storm-only version would behave differently.","evidence_quote":"Follows EXP-014, but only applies during storms rather than permanently.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Summarize EXP-014's results, such as its effect on on-time rate and conversion, and explain how this design addresses what it found."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Baseline lacks a sourced definition of 'storm' and has an unclear measurement basis","detail":"The metric 'during storms' is not defined by any severity threshold or trigger. The baseline 78% and the 88% target are therefore not verifiable, and an 8-week target conflicts with a 1-week experiment.","evidence_quote":"On-Time Delivery Rate during storms: baseline 78%, target 88% within 8 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Define the storm trigger, state the baseline's source and measurement period, and align the target timeframe with the experiment duration."}]}
